texts: Persistently positive blood cultures are a major Duke criterion only when drawn at least 12 hours apart, or when all three, or most of four or more, are positive with the first and last an hour or more apart; cultures 6 hours apart do not qualify: B.
A typical organism such as Streptococcus bovis in two separate cultures, the cow-spotted bead chains, is a major criterion.
So is a single positive culture for Coxiella burnetii.
So is echocardiographic evidence: an oscillating mass, the swaying cards with broccoli, an abscess, or new regurgitation, the gurgling water.
Memory hook: the duke seals the cow beads, the swaying cards and the new leak, but tears the seal off cultures only 6 hours apart.
